summary: Intermittent GPU starvation causing request fallback chains and aggressive queue thinning in dedicated cluster
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:10 UTC VectorHealth reported sustained 5-10% request failures and large latency tails from their dedicated tenant in us-west-2. Impact: customer production inference pipelines experienced elevated P99 latency (2-5x baseline) and sporadic request routing to lower-cost fallback model variants, causing reduced output quality. Environment: Redwood Dedicated cluster gdc-usw2-12 serving VectorHealth reserved pool (8xA100 nodes) with autoscaler enabled and burst capacity off. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send steady 10 RPS traffic mix of 1k token prompts to gptx-7b pinned model. 2) Observe queue length and scheduler logs over 30 minutes. 3) Correlate with node GPU utilisation and host-level telemetry. Observed behavior: - Autoscaler did not add nodes despite queue growth, instead scheduler started preemptively re-routing requests to lower-cost quantized model variants (fallback chain). - Several nodes reported transient GPU allocation failures and out-of-memory reclaim events; these nodes also showed higher-than-expected kernel eviction counts. - Request admission controller applied aggressive queue thinning (rejecting or re-routing ~12% of requests) to maintain latency SLO. Expected behavior: Autoscaler should spin up burst capacity or notify ops before fallback routing; GPU allocation errors should be isolated to misbehaving pods or noisy tenants rather than causing cluster-wide admission control changes. Logs/metrics attached below and in linked dashboards.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use VectorHealth test harness to replay steady 10 RPS of 1k-token prompts against tenant pool
2) Monitor /metrics/queue_length and autoscaler decisions for 30 minutes
3) Pull kernel-level GPU logs (nvidia-smi nvlink, dmesg) on nodes reporting allocation failures
4) Verify fallback routing events in request-trace logs in the console
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant on same pool causing higher memory pressure and kernel preemptions -> cascade into allocation failures.
Checked node metrics: nodes n02 and n03 have elevated GPU memory fragmentation and higher kernel eviction counts compared to baseline.
Autoscaler logs show 'policy_min_uptime' prevented immediate scale-up; cluster was configured with conservative burst settings for this dedicated pool.
Correlated with customer traffic: VectorHealth workload includes occasional long-sequence prompts (1k tokens) that increase KV cache pressure and reduce effective batch density.
Observed that fallback routing logic treats repeated allocation errors as cluster-level capacity signals and triggers lower-accuracy model variants rather than per-tenant isolation.
Checked cloud provider capacity: no region-wide GPU shortage events reported; problem localized to the tenant pool due to bin-packing of noisy pods.
comments: [2026-03-10 09:01] Support (Aisha): Thanks for the report — we've started triage and pulled the last 6 hours of metrics. Can you confirm if any long-running jobs were added to the pool around 07:50 UTC?

[2026-03-10 09:12] Customer (VectorHealth - James Lee): No scheduled jobs were changed. We did run an A/B eval ramp at 07:45 that increased prompt length, but it was targeted to their staging cluster; nothing should have hit production.

[2026-03-10 10:05] Eng (Miguel): Found 2 nodes with repeated allocation errors and high kernel eviction counts. Suspect cross-tenant bin-packing causing fragmentation. Recommending temporary tenant isolation and a restart of the offending serving pods.
[2026-03-10 10:22] SRE (Li Wen): Implemented temporary soft-isolation: tainted 2 nodes and evicted non-reserved pods; scaled reserved pool by +2 nodes as emergency mitigation.
[2026-03-10 11:00] Support (Aisha): After the mitigation, VectorHealth reports P99 latency returned to baseline and fallback routing stopped. We're monitoring for recurrence over 24h.

[2026-03-12 14:10] Eng (Miguel): Root cause analysis complete — noisy tenant's long-sequence evals created fragmented GPU memory; autoscaler policy prevented rapid burst. Patch submitted to autoscaler to relax burst gating when allocation errors exceed threshold (PR #210).
[2026-03-12 14:20] Customer (James Lee): Thanks — glad to see a plan. Please share any long-term recommendations for pool sizing and isolation.
resolution: Mitigation: 1) Immediate: tainted and evacuated misbehaving nodes, added +2 emergency nodes to VectorHealth reserved pool, restarted serving pods for clean GPU allocation. 2) Short-term fix: adjusted autoscaler policy to allow emergency burst on repeated allocation errors and added a threshold to trigger per-tenant isolation rather than global fallback routing. 3) Long-term: engineering to add GPU memory fragmentation metrics to autoscaler signals and introduce tenant-aware bin-packing. Follow-ups: create an alert for 'allocation_error_rate > 5% over 5m', update Dedicated capacity runbook to include noisy-tenant isolation steps, and schedule capacity review with VectorHealth in two weeks.

Add fragmentation and kernel-eviction metrics to tenant dashboards
